transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-01-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Platform: Zoom
Attendees: Aaron Kim, Priya Patel, Sofia Martinez (Redwood) - Liam O'Connor, Mei Zhang, Rajnish Kapoor, Aisha Bello (EmeraldWave)

00:00:03 - Aaron Kim: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the packaging checklist.
00:00:18 - Liam O'Connor: Hey Aaron, hey Priya, thanks. We're excited to get this into the marketplace, there's a bunch of compliance boxes to tick so want to make sure this is aligned.
00:00:30 - Priya Patel: Great, we'll start with an overview of the listing artifacts and then dig into VPC/onprem integration.
00:00:45 - Priya Patel: So, high level - Redwood expects a Helm chart, a lightweight adapter for VPC connectivity, KMS integration points, and a billing metering connector for marketplace usage. We'll walk through each.
00:01:05 - Mei Zhang: Quick question - the billing connector, is that push-based or do you support pull-based usage export?
00:01:15 - Aaron Kim: It's typically a push-based webhook to the marketplace meter, but there's also an S3 export path we can wire up. Depends on your security posture.
00:01:32 - Mei Zhang: Okay, we prefer S3 export with signed uploads for compliance.
00:01:40 - Priya Patel: Noted. For VPC there are two patterns we've seen: 1) direct VPC peering with our listing connector inside your VPC; 2) a hosted connector with an egress IP allowlist. For regulated workloads you mostly want the former.
00:02:00 - Rajnish Kapoor: We definitely prefer peering or private link. We need to keep traffic inside the corp network - egress policies are tricky. Also need KMS keys under our control.
00:02:15 - Sofia Martinez: Totally understood. We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and bring-your-own HSM in some cases). There may be additional logging you'll want - we can enable audit logs for every model call.
00:02:32 - Rajnish Kapoor: When you say audit logs, what fields are recorded? We need request_id, model_id, timestamp, token metadata, and a hash of the prompt to avoid storing plaintext.
00:02:45 - Priya Patel: Right now we capture request_id, model_id, duration, and raw token counts. For sensitive workloads, we can enable prompt hashing, redaction hooks, and disable full prompt storage. We'll follow up with the exact schema.
00:03:05 - Liam O'Connor: Can you point to an example schema? It's important for our SOC2 audit.
00:03:12 - Aaron Kim: We'll push the audit schema doc after the call — link in the notes.
00:03:20 - Aisha Bello: On the packaging front, how opinionated is the Helm chart — can we set resource limits and custom node selectors?
00:03:30 - Priya Patel: Yes the chart exposes values for nodeSelectors, tolerations, GPU instance types, and autoscaling policies. We'll also provide a sample values.yaml tuned for small dev clusters.
00:03:45 - Mei Zhang: Sweet. On quantization and model variants — we run some workloads that are latency sensitive and some that are cost sensitive. How do you recommend mapping model variants to the marketplace SKU?
00:04:00 - Priya Patel: We recommend offering two SKUs: a "low-latency" SKU backed by fp16 or int8 optimized runtime with reserved dedicated capacity, and a "cost-optimized" SKU using a quantized model variant. The runtime will auto-select kernels based on seq length distribution.
00:04:20 - Mei Zhang: Does Redwood handle automatic fallback if the dedicated pool is saturated?
00:04:25 - Aaron Kim: Yes, there's a smart routing policy that can fallback to a compatible hosted variant; it's configurable per listing. Important to set explicit SLOs so the app knows what to expect.
00:04:38 - Rajnish Kapoor: In the fallback case, what about data residency and encryption?
00:04:45 - Priya Patel: Fallback still respects encryption and KMS; however, for residency we have region-aware routing so we won't cross region boundaries unless configured. We'll document that in the rollout plan.
00:04:58 - 00:05:12 - [crosstalk, inaudible] Laughter and brief digression about holiday schedules
00:05:20 - Priya Patel: Back to packaging — the Helm chart will include a CRD for listing metadata, container images with proper imagePullSecrets, and a preflight job that validates connectivity to your KMS and VPC endpoints.
00:05:38 - Liam O'Connor: We need the preflight to fail safely and produce a clear remediation path. Our ops team will run it in CI.
00:05:47 - Priya Patel: Absolutely. We'll include exit codes and a troubleshooting doc.
00:05:55 - Aaron Kim: Can we talk about benchmarks? We recommended a micro-benchmark for 128-token chat and 512-token batch gen — measuring p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
00:06:10 - Mei Zhang: Yes, we can run that. We'll need guidance on traffic shaping and the exact request shapes.
00:06:18 - Priya Patel: We'll share a bench harness (link to github.com/redwood/bench-harness) with example scripts. Expect that the harness will simulate KV cache warm-up and varying seq lengths.
00:06:33 - Mei Zhang: Will the harness run against a quantized runtime? We want to see where accuracy vs cost crosses.
00:06:40 - Priya Patel: It can — we support toggling quantization flags. Quick note: quantization sometimes changes tokenization boundary behavior slightly, so include a small eval set to check regressions.
00:06:53 - Rajnish Kapoor: On security controls: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC — how granular can we get for teams within EmeraldWave?
00:07:02 - Sofia Martinez: We support SAML SSO integration and SCIM provisioning. On RBAC we expose roles down to route-level permissions and token-scoped keys. We'll provide a mapping guide for enterprise roles.
00:07:16 - Aisha Bello: Good. For the marketplace listing, are there specific SLA/metering expectations that could block certification?
00:07:25 - Aaron Kim: The marketplace requires a documented SLA for uptime and latency for listed SKUs. They also want clear billing unit definitions. We'll help draft the listing page language.
00:07:36 - Mei Zhang: Also curious about canary/rollout: can we stage traffic across tenants? We want to A/B a config change for tokenization and compare regressions.
00:07:47 - Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-customer canary rules and canary % by route. You can route 10% of traffic to a canary variant and run automatic regression checks against eval prompts.
00:08:03 - Liam O'Connor: That eval check, is it automated or manual?
00:08:07 - Priya Patel: We can automate with your prompt set; it runs an eval job and alerts on quality regressions. It's part of Redwood Optimize.
00:08:15 - Aaron Kim: Quick pause — any blockers on the security side before we proceed?
00:08:21 - Rajnish Kapoor: KMS key rotation policy and proof of HSM if we request it. Also a list of required log events to pass audit.
00:08:30 - Sofia Martinez: We'll provide the KMS accreditation matrix and the audit events doc.
00:08:37 - 00:09:05 - [brief silence]
00:09:06 - Priya Patel: Switching gears — networking specifics. For peering we need your VPC CIDR ranges, a set of allowed ports and the egress ip range. We can provision a small BGP session if you want a private link approach.
00:09:24 - Mei Zhang: We'll share CIDRs; do you support IPv6?
00:09:28 - Priya Patel: Fully support IPv6 for endpoints, though the listing connector defaults to IPv4; we can enable dual-stack.
00:09:36 - Liam O'Connor: Any special kernel or driver requirements on our side for GPU runtimes?
00:09:42 - Priya Patel: The runtime uses standard CUDA stacks for NVIDIA and ROCm for AMD. We're also shipping quantized kernels that prefer compute capability 7.5+. We'll include a node labeling guide.
00:09:56 - Mei Zhang: If we want to run on a mixed cluster, can we pin certain deployments to GPU nodes only?
00:10:03 - Priya Patel: Yes, chart supports nodeAffinity per component.
00:10:08 - Aaron Kim: On billing - EmeraldWave wants S3-based metering; we'll map S3 manifests to marketplace usage, with a reconciliation job. Note small discrepancy windows may exist.
00:10:21 - Mei Zhang: That's fine. We'll account for reconciliation.
00:10:26 - Aisha Bello: I also wanted to confirm support for offline/on-prem air-gapped install — what's the current status?
00:10:34 - Sofia Martinez: We have an on-prem package with an offline bundle and signing keys. For air-gapped installs we require a manual attestation and a sandboxed signer. It's heavier lift but supported for enterprise.
00:10:48 - Rajnish Kapoor: We'll likely need that for some regulated customers.
00:10:52 - Aaron Kim: Good note. We'll include the attestation checklist in the marketplace docs.
00:10:58 - 00:11:12 - [typing noise]
00:11:13 - Priya Patel: Ok, let's walk through a proposed timeline: this week — exchange perf traces and Helm PR; next week — run bench and preflight; week after — marketplace preflight cert. Does that sound workable?
00:11:30 - Liam O'Connor: Yes. We can provide perf traces by Friday.
00:11:35 - Mei Zhang: We'll also run a quick dev install using the sample values file.
00:11:40 - Aaron Kim: Perfect. I'll send the checklist and bench harness link after the call.
00:11:47 - Aisha Bello: One more question — are there any IP / redistributor clauses we should be aware of in the marketplace agreement?
00:11:55 - Aaron Kim: For listings we have standard marketplace terms; if you need a reseller carveout we can loop legal.
00:12:04 - Rajnish Kapoor: Can you share the marketplace terms summary?
00:12:07 - Aaron Kim: Yes, we'll attach a one-pager.
00:12:12 - Priya Patel: Quick call-out on observability: the console exposes token-level latency, model-level cost, and per-tenant traces. We also ship Prometheus metrics for your telemetry.
00:12:25 - Mei Zhang: Prometheus is good. Can we also forward traces to our tracing backend (we use Lightstep)?
00:12:32 - Sofia Martinez: Yes, you can dry-run an OTEL exporter to Lightstep. We'll include an example config.
00:12:40 - 00:12:58 - [15s pause while someone reviews a doc]
00:12:59 - Priya Patel: Anything else on the technical side?
00:13:05 - Mei Zhang: One more — model version pinning. We want to ensure a pinned model doesn't auto-upgrade.
00:13:11 - Priya Patel: Customers can pin model versions per route and we support rollout windows with automatic rollback on regressions.
00:13:20 - Aaron Kim: Great. If no other blockers, let's confirm owners of the action items.
00:13:25 - Priya Patel: Action item recap — Priya will produce Helm values and a sample values.yaml; Aaron will share the packaging checklist and marketplace doc; Mei will provide perf traces; Rajnish will share KMS details.
00:13:38 - Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the traces and cluster details posted to the shared drive by Friday.
00:13:46 - Aaron Kim: Perfect. We'll schedule the preflight the week of Jan 23rd. I'll follow up with a calendar invite.
00:13:56 - Aisha Bello: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
00:14:00 - Aaron Kim: Thanks all, we'll close there.

[Call ends at 16:57 UTC]
